verification_report.summary:
The complete chapter is correct under the expressly accepted inputs. Seventeen sequential statement checks and five reference/dependency records found no critical errors or gaps. Both initially pending prerequisite reports, prescribed_lp_existence_01 and common_barrier_repair_01, are now complete with verdict correct. Earlier deep inputs were checked for scope and use rather than re-audited. The book was left unchanged.

Order and concavity use singular strict domination with the correct orientation: the solution with the smaller proposed scalar is the first potential, and an arbitrary constant translate of the comparison potential is second. Ordinary equivalence supplies both the singularity order and a genuine smaller-background competitor. Translation, essential-infimum/supremum bounds, and Lipschitz signs are correct. The singular density lemma applies the accepted bounded mixed inequality to admissible semipositive truncations, expands with positive binomial coefficients, and uses plurifine locality on common finite levels. Increasing exhaustion proves the measure inequality without unrestricted truncation convergence, finite total mass, or subtraction of infinities. Weighted arithmetic-geometric mean then gives concavity.

For bounded-L1 continuity, scalar order bounds give a fixed smooth-volume domination of the solution measures. The relative uniform estimate supplies common barriers after supremum normalization. Canonical compactness and the accepted dominated common-barrier corollary give a genuine limit of the same ordinary type and raw weak measure convergence. Uniform boundedness makes the exponential Lipschitz, so the equation densities converge in total variation. Scalar uniqueness identifies every subsequential scalar limit and proves convergence of the entire scalar sequence. No uniqueness or full-sequence convergence of potentials is needed.

The infinite-dimensional support argument is valid. For C=-B on all of C(X), the directional derivative is finite, sublinear and bounded by the uniform norm. Dominated Hahn-Banach therefore gives a linear functional whose continuity follows by testing both signs. Translation forces its value on one to be one, and monotonicity forces positivity. Riesz gives a countably additive regular Borel probability. The support inequalities define a convex closed subset of the compact probability space for the weak-star, or narrow, topology. Compact metrizability of X justifies the subsequent subsequence arguments.

The absolute-continuity inference has the required direction: for a cutoff chi equal to one on a compact volume-null set K, the support inequality gives nu(K)<=integral chi dnu<=B(F)-B(F+chi). Cutoffs with shrinking support volume converge to zero in L1 while remaining uniformly bounded. Bounded-L1 continuity makes the last difference tend to zero. Inner regularity extends vanishing from compact null sets to every Borel null set, and Radon-Nikodym supplies the probability density. No Lp bound with p>1 is asserted. Absolute continuity of limits of smooth adjoint probabilities follows from their membership in the limiting support set, not from weak convergence alone.

Uniform stability follows by passing each continuous support inequality to the limit. Supports at F bound the right derivative above, while supports at F+tG bound it below; compactness and stability give exactly the negative maximum. Replacing G by -G gives the negative minimum for the left derivative. Singleton support is therefore equivalent to Gateaux differentiability, with derivative G mapped to minus its integral. No Frechet differentiability is inferred.

The book's accepted smooth derivative theorem uses precisely a Hermitian background, a strictly positive smooth solution metric, and arbitrary fixed smooth positive dV. Scalar uniqueness identifies its b with B_0. Testing both signs of smooth variations and using uniform density of smooth functions identifies the entire support set with the normalized Gauduchon adjoint. Dimension one is correctly treated by Stokes. In the closed Kahler case, SGPT Definition 1.5.2, Proposition 2.2.2 and Theorem 2.4.3 match the exact ordinary singularity relation and provide finite mass invariance; positivity also follows from the equation at F=0. The required arXiv search was followed by web fallback and direct manuscript checking, with corroboration in [Witt Nystrom, Definition 1.1 and Theorem 1.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1703.01950). Integration gives the stated logarithmic formula, and differentiation gives the unique exponential probability.

Every geometric hypothesis has a justified role. No BMP, PVP, uniqueness of normalized weak potentials, distributional weak adjoint identity, or primitive for the raw Monge-Ampere one-form is used or claimed. Collins21 remains context only. The concluding questions assert neither novelty nor verified open status.
